# Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars) collects the run's telemetry to the local JSONL
sink whenever the share-telemetry setting is on, and collects nothing when the setting is off
or in a production build.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically collect its run
telemetry, so the run can be evaluated without a manual export step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `resolveEffectiveTelemetryConfig()` (with the settings-driven flag wired in) returns
  `recording: true` with sink `jsonl` when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true and
  `shareTelemetryDev` is true, with **no** `VITE_TELEMETRY_*` env vars set.
- In dev with `shareTelemetryDev === false`, recording is disabled — the game neither collects
  nor uploads (parent AC2). **Plan-time decision:** the setting is the controlling gate for dev
  collection; the env-var escape hatch remains available for production (where it still requires
  consent), and this ordering is asserted by tests.
- In a production build (`PROD === true`) behaviour is unchanged: recording still requires
  `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` plus the consent flag; `shareTelemetryDev` is ignored.
- `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` loads the persisted setting and passes the dev-collection flag
  into config resolution, so a fresh dev session records from run start.
- Unit tests cover the (dev/prod) × (on/off) matrix plus production-consent-unchanged regression,
  and the JSONL sink writes under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` in the happy-dom test env.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/telemetry/config.ts` (and `consent.ts` resolution) with an optional
  `devCollectionEnabled` flag derived from the setting; default `false` so existing callers and
  production envs are unchanged.
- Change the effective recording gate to `DEV ? (setting || existing-resolved-recording) :
  existing-resolved-recording`, keeping the consent path intact — the exact boolean composition is
  pinned by the tests above.
- Update `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` (~line 3872) to `loadSettings()` and pass
  `settings.shareTelemetryDev`.
- Tests in `config.test.ts`, `consent.test.ts` and the PlayScene suite.

**Key Files:**

- `src/telemetry/config.ts`
- `src/telemetry/consent.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/telemetry/config.test.ts`
- `src/telemetry/consent.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (dev gate helper) and F2 (setting field) — collection gating composes with both.

## Deliverables

Dev-gated collection-on-by-default + matrix tests; production behaviour provably unchanged.

# Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player — Intake Brief

## Headline

Expose the ship's existing control schemes (`fourDirectional`, `asteroids`) as a
player-facing, persisted setting in `SettingsScene`, backed by a per-player
`controlScheme` field in `ai_hell_settings` that overrides the shared
`ship-config.csv` default. The list of choices is data-driven so future schemes
appear automatically, and the choice applies from the next run.

## Problem Statement

The player's control scheme is currently a **shared, repo-level** value
(`ShipConfig.controlScheme` in `src/data/ship-config.csv`, default
`asteroids`). Only the Player gym — and only in a dev build — can change it, and
saving writes back to the repo CSV for *everyone*. There is no in-game,
player-facing way to pick a scheme: a player who prefers direct
four-directional movement cannot switch.

## Users

- **Player who prefers four-directional movement** — wants direct WASD thrust
  instead of Asteroids turn-and-thrust, chosen in Settings and remembered.
- **Player who prefers Asteroids movement** — wants the shipped default but the
  freedom to switch, with the choice held across sessions.
- **Developer adding a future scheme** — wants a new `ControlScheme` member to
  show up in the setting without hand-editing UI code.

### User stories

- As a player, I want to choose my control scheme in the Settings screen so the
  ship handles the way I expect, without editing the repo.
- As a player, I want my chosen scheme remembered next time I launch the game
  so I do not have to re-select it every run.
- As a developer, I want the scheme list driven by the `ControlScheme` type so
  a newly added scheme is selectable without new UI wiring.

## Existing State

- `ControlScheme = 'fourDirectional' | 'asteroids'` (`src/core/configTypes.ts:348`),
  mirrored as `ControlSchemeType` in `src/utils/movementModel.ts:20`.
- `ShipConfig.controlScheme` is persisted globally in
  `src/data/ship-config.csv`; built-in default is `'asteroids'`
  (`src/core/configDefaults.ts:598`).
- `Player` applies `ship.controlScheme` at construction
  (`src/entities/Player.ts:337`) and `setConfig()` swaps scheme live
  (`src/entities/Player.ts:614`).
- Input dispatch is scheme-keyed in exactly one place:
  `mapControlInput(scheme, raw)` (`src/utils/movementModel.ts:569`), consumed by
  `CombatCoreScene._readPlayerInput` and the gyms (`GymPlayer`) — this is the
  gym↔game parity seam.
- Player-facing settings live in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (localStorage
  `ai_hell_settings`: SFX volume/mute, key bindings, dev telemetry sharing) and
  are edited in `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts`, reachable from `MenuScene` and
  `PauseScene`. Its Controls section renders one row per `ActionName` with
  shared binding values.
- Ship-config writes go through a dev-only CSV plugin
  (`src/core/configStore.ts:628`); production builds read the bundled CSV
  read-only.
- The GDD already states the ship "honours the player's **saved control
  scheme**" (GDD §2.2), but the only save path today is the gym/dev CSV.

## Desired Change

- Add a validated `controlScheme` field to the persisted settings record
  (`ai_hell_settings`) defaulting to today's shipped behaviour (`'asteroids'`),
  with legacy/corrupt records falling back safely. This is the **per-player
  override**; `ship-config.csv` stays the designer-owned default and is never
  written from the settings UI.
- Add a focusable **Control Scheme** row to `SettingsScene`'s Controls section
  (Left/Right cycles, pointer click activates, keyboard-navigable like the
  existing rows) driven by a single ordered list derived from the
  `ControlScheme` union.
- Resolve the **effective player scheme** through one helper with explicit
  precedence: player setting → ship config `controlScheme` → built-in default.
- Apply the resolved scheme to the player ship in `PlayScene` when the ship is
  created, so a change takes effect on the **next run / next ship spawn** and
  never mid-run; the gyms keep their own scheme toggle.
- Relabel the Controls-section movement rows for the selected scheme (Asteroids:
  **Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse**) while keeping one shared set of
  bindings across schemes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Setting exists and is data-driven:** SettingsScene shows a Control Scheme control whose options are derived from the `ControlScheme` union (no hard-coded per-scheme UI branch), displaying the current value.
- **AC2 — Persistence and fallback:** Changing the scheme persists it in `ai_hell_settings` and is restored on the next load; a legacy record without the field, a non-string value, or a value outside the union resolves to the default (`asteroids`). Unit-tested in `settingsStore`.
- **AC3 — Precedence:** a single resolution helper returns the stored setting when present and valid; otherwise the ship config `controlScheme`; otherwise the built-in default. Unit tests cover all three levels and the never-mutates-the-config guarantee.
- **AC4 — Applied in game at the next spawn:** `PlayScene` creates the player with the resolved scheme, verified by a scene test that a saved `fourDirectional` setting drives four-directional input (and a saved `asteroids` setting drives Asteroids input), without mutating `ship-config.csv` or the loaded ship-config object. A change made mid-run does not alter the current run's ship.
- **AC5 — Keyboard and pointer operable:** the row is reachable via the existing focus order, changeable with Left/Right and Enter/click, and the selected value is announced in the row text.
- **AC6 — Controls rows reflect the scheme:** under Asteroids the movement rows read **Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse** and under four-directional they read **Move Up / Move Down / Move Left / Move Right**; both schemes keep the same single binding set (no per-scheme binding storage).
- **AC7 — Parity preserved:** the gym scheme toggle still works, scheme→input mapping still lives only in `mapControlInput`, and the gym→game parity guards (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, gym-parity docs assertion) pass.
- **AC8 — Tests:** new/updated unit and scene tests cover each of AC1–AC7 (settings round-trip/fallback, resolution helper, SettingsScene control and relabelling, `PlayScene` application).
- **AC9 — Documentation:** the GDD (§2.2 controls and §6.6 save-data `ai_hell_settings` row) — and `README.md` where it summarises controls — describe the new setting and the player-setting-over-config precedence.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The choice is **per-player** (local to the browser/device via
  `ai_hell_settings`), not the shared designer config; `src/data/ship-config.csv`
  remains the shipped/default source and must not be written from the settings
  UI.
- No new movement physics: reuse `mapControlInput` and the existing
  `FourDirectionalInputHandler` / `AsteroidsInputHandler`.
- Settings must remain fully keyboard operable (no mouse required).
- Backwards compatible: existing `ai_hell_settings` records keep working
  without migration.
- Do not force a scheme in gyms (they are tuning tools with their own toggle).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — add `controlScheme` to `SettingsRecord`, a
  default, and validation/fallback in `loadSettings`.
- `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` — round-trip plus legacy/corrupt fallback.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` — new focusable Control Scheme row, cycle
  handling, scheme-aware row labels, `_persist()` update, accessors for tests.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts` — row presence, cycling through all
  schemes, persistence, relabelling.
- `src/core/config.ts` (or a small new helper module, e.g.
  `src/core/playerScheme.ts`) — single exported resolution helper with the
  documented precedence.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — resolve and apply the scheme when creating the
  player ship.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — only if a scheme-only override is needed beyond
  the existing `setScheme()`/config path.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md` — document the setting.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Two sources of truth** (shared CSV vs per-player setting). *Mitigation:*
  explicit documented precedence, one resolution helper, settings never write
  the CSV.
- **Gym↔game parity guard.** *Mitigation:* keep scheme→input mapping solely in
  `mapControlInput`; gyms stay config/toggle-driven.
- **Binding semantics under Asteroids** (`Move Down` is reverse thrust,
  `Move Left/Right` are turn). *Mitigation:* relabel rows per scheme (AC6) while
  keeping the shared binding set.
- **Mid-run switching.** *Avoided by design:* AC4 applies the scheme at the next
  ship spawn.
- **Scope creep** — per-scheme key bindings, per-scheme tunables in Settings,
  adding a third scheme. *Out of scope;* record as linked follow-up items.
- **Assumption:** the setting is local to the device (localStorage) and the
  control lists itself from the union, not from ship config.
- **Assumption:** no telemetry/schema change is required.

## Related Work

- `AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T` — Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme
  (completed) — establishes `asteroids` as the shipped default this setting
  must preserve.
- `AH-0MUA8BEUR006RWCI` — SettingsScene: SFX volume slider + mute toggle
  (completed) — the settings-row pattern to follow.
- `AH-0MUA8BGE0006UAU4` — SettingsScene: key-binding remapping + reset to
  defaults (completed) — Controls section and focus order.
- `AH-0MUA8BK1E001UZUC` — Apply rebindable keys to gameplay and menus
  (completed) — how persisted settings reach `PlayScene`.
- `AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N` — MenuScene Settings button (completed) and
  `AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292` — In-game menu (completed) — entry points.
- `AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD` — Alternative player control (completed) — original
  Asteroids scheme.
- `AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0` — Shared player-control step across all scenes
  (completed) — the single `mapControlInput` seam.
- `AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V` — Ship config `controlScheme` does not survive a game
  server restart (completed) — why CSV writes are brittle.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.2 (controls), §6.6 (`ai_hell_settings`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N** – MenuScene Settings button (completed)
- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed)
- **AH-0MUCG5T7S001F9MQ** – Keep asteroids moving and collidable during the transition (Phase 2) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, allow, asteroids, available, change (+9 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, allow, asteroids, available, change (+9 more)
- `README.md` — matched: add, allow, asteroids, available, change (+8 more)

## Decisions (confirmed by producer)

1. **Storage & precedence** — (a) per-player `controlScheme` in
   `ai_hell_settings`, overriding the ship config for the player; the CSV stays
   the designer/shipped default.
2. **Apply timing** — (a) next run / next ship spawn; never mid-run.
3. **Controls-section semantics** — (a) relabel rows per scheme only; one shared
   binding set across schemes.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Storage and precedence.** "Where should the player's chosen scheme be
  stored, and what overrides what? (a) New per-player `controlScheme` field in
  `ai_hell_settings` (localStorage), used by the player ship in preference to
  the ship config; `ship-config.csv` stays the designer default.
  (b) Write through to the shared `src/data/ship-config.csv` (dev builds only).
  (c) Both: local override plus an optional 'save as project default' action."
  — **Recommended:** (a). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** —
  per-player setting overrides the config; the CSV remains the designer default.
  Source: operator reply in the intake resumption session (2026-10-21).

- **Q2 — Apply timing.** "When a player changes the scheme, when should it take
  effect? (a) On the next run / next ship spawn (the current run keeps its
  scheme, with a short 'applies next run' note). (b) Immediately, mid-run, via
  `Player.setScheme()`." — **Recommended:** (a). — **Answer (producer,
  interactive reply): (a)** — applies on the next run/ship spawn, never
  mid-run. Source: operator reply in the intake resumption session (2026-10-21).

- **Q3 — Controls-section semantics.** "In the Controls section, should the
  movement rows change with the selected scheme? (a) Relabel only: under
  Asteroids show 'Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse', but bindings stay
  shared across schemes. (b) Relabel and keep separate bindings per scheme.
  (c) Leave the existing labels unchanged." — **Recommended:** (a). —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — relabel only; bindings remain
  shared across schemes. Source: operator reply in the intake resumption
  session (2026-10-21).

## Goal

As a developer, I need failing-first unit tests that pin the persisted
`controlScheme` contract and the effective-scheme precedence before the
production code exists, so the settings field and resolution helper are driven
by tests (TDD).

## Scope

Add unit tests only — no production changes in this item:

1. `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` — `controlScheme` in `ai_hell_settings`:
   - the default record exposes `controlScheme: 'asteroids'` when nothing is saved;
   - save → load round-trips both `'asteroids'` and `'fourDirectional'` and leaves the other settings untouched;
   - a legacy record without the field resolves to `'asteroids'` and preserves volume/mute/bindings/telemetry;
   - a non-string value (number, `null`, object) resolves to `'asteroids'`;
   - a value outside the union (e.g. `'orbital'`) resolves to `'asteroids'`.
2. `src/core/playerScheme.test.ts` (new) — the effective-scheme resolution helper:
   - a valid stored setting wins over the ship-config `controlScheme`;
   - an absent/invalid stored setting falls back to the ship-config value;
   - both absent/invalid falls back to the built-in default (`'asteroids'`);
   - the helper never mutates the ship-config object (deep-equal snapshot before/after) and performs no CSV write.

Reference the existing fallback patterns (`resolveBindings`, corrupt-JSON
fallback) in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` for style.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New/updated unit and scene tests cover each of AC1–AC7 (settings round-trip/fallback, resolution helper, SettingsScene control and relabelling, `PlayScene` application) — this item owns its share of parent AC8 and the sibling test item owns the rest.
- Settings-store unit tests assert the default `controlScheme` is `asteroids`, that a saved value is restored, and that legacy, non-string and out-of-union values fall back to `asteroids` — covering the persistence and fallback requirement in full.
- Resolution-helper unit tests assert all three precedence levels (stored setting → ship config `controlScheme` → built-in default) and that the ship config is never mutated.
- Tests fail for the expected reason before items "Persist player control scheme in settings" and "Resolve effective player control scheme" land (red), then pass (green) after them.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope) — never an ad-hoc runner invocation.

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` — controlScheme round-trip, legacy/corrupt fallback cases.
- `src/core/playerScheme.test.ts` — new spec for the precedence helper.

## Constraints

- Test-only change: no production code in this item.
- Follow the existing vitest style and helpers already used in `settingsStore.test.ts`.
- Use UK English in descriptions and comments.

## Definition of done

- The new tests exist, are wired into the existing suites, and are red for the right reasons.
- `/skill:test` (changed scope) has been run and the red state is recorded in a comment.

## Parent AC coverage

Covers parent AC2 (persistence and fallback, test half), AC3 (precedence, test half)
and AC8 (tests) from "Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player".

## Goal

As a player, I want my chosen control scheme remembered between sessions so the
ship handles the way I expect without editing the repo.

Add a persisted, validated per-player `controlScheme` field to the
`ai_hell_settings` record. This is the per-player override; the designer-owned
`src/data/ship-config.csv` is never written from settings.

## Scope

- Add `controlScheme: ControlScheme` to `SettingsRecord` in `src/core/settingsStore.ts`.
- Add `controlScheme: 'asteroids'` to `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` (today's shipped
  default, established by AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T).
- Add a single ordered, readonly `CONTROL_SCHEMES` list (and a type guard)
  derived from the `ControlScheme` union so the Settings UI can iterate it
  without hard-coded per-scheme branches — a future scheme added to the union
  becomes selectable automatically.
- Validate in `loadSettings`: missing field, non-string, blank or
  out-of-union values fall back to the default; valid values are preserved.
- Persist through the existing `saveSettings` path; keep the existing
  corrupt-JSON and storage-unavailable fallbacks intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SettingsRecord` exposes `controlScheme` and `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.controlScheme` is `asteroids`.
- Saving a setting persists `controlScheme` in `ai_hell_settings` and a subsequent load restores it, leaving all other settings unchanged.
- A legacy record without the field, a non-string value, or a value outside the union resolves to `asteroids`.
- An ordered option list (`CONTROL_SCHEMES`) is exported from the settings module and is derived from the `ControlScheme` union (no per-scheme UI branching).
- `src/data/ship-config.csv` and the ship-config store are untouched by this module.
- Unit tests (from the test item) pass; `/skill:test` changed scope is green.

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — record field, default, validation, ordered scheme list.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing `loadSettings` merge-over-defaults and validation style; no new storage backend.
- Backwards compatible: existing `ai_hell_settings` records keep working with no migration step.
- Never import the ship-config store here — settings must not depend on, or write, the CSV.

## Definition of done

- Tests from "Test: settings and scheme-resolution unit tests" pass for the settings half.
- A comment records the commit and the changed files.

## Parent AC coverage

Covers parent AC2 (persistence and fallback) and the data-driven option-list half
of AC1 from "Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player".

## Dependencies

Blocked by the settings unit-test item (test-first).

data.description:
## Goal

As a developer, I want one helper that decides the player's effective control
scheme so the two sources of truth (per-player setting and designer CSV) have a
single, documented precedence and the game cannot drift from it.

## Scope

Create `src/core/playerScheme.ts` exporting a small pure resolver:

```
resolvePlayerControlScheme(stored: SettingsRecord | undefined, shipConfig: ShipConfig | undefined): ControlScheme
```

Documented precedence: valid stored player setting → ship-config
`controlScheme` → built-in default (`'asteroids'`). The helper must be pure: it
never mutates the settings record or the passed ship config, and never touches
the CSV store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single exported resolution helper returns the stored setting when present and valid; otherwise the ship config `controlScheme`; otherwise the built-in default.
- The helper never mutates the supplied ship-config object and performs no CSV write (unit-tested with a before/after deep-equal snapshot).
- Invalid or absent inputs degrade to the next precedence level rather than throwing, including a ship config with a missing or unrecognised `controlScheme`.
- Unit tests from the test item pass; the module is imported only where the effective player scheme is needed (no behaviour change in gyms).

## Key Files

- `src/core/playerScheme.ts` — new pure resolver module.

## Constraints

- Pure function, no Phaser or storage imports beyond type-only imports.
- No new movement physics and no change to `mapControlInput` — the resolver only chooses the scheme value.
- Use UK English in comments and docs.

## Definition of done

- Tests from "Test: settings and scheme-resolution unit tests" pass for the resolution half.
- A comment records the commit and the changed files.

## Parent AC coverage

Covers parent AC3 (precedence via a single resolution helper) from
"Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player".

## Dependencies

Blocked by the settings unit-test item and by "Persist player control scheme in
settings" (needs the validated record field).

## Goal

As a developer, I need failing-first scene tests that pin the SettingsScene
control-scheme UI and the `PlayScene` application behaviour before the UI and
scene code changes land, so AC1/AC4/AC5/AC6 are test-driven end to end.

## Scope

Add scene tests only — no production changes in this item:

1. `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts`:
   - a Control Scheme row exists in the Controls section and is reachable through the existing focus order;
   - Left/Right cycles the scheme in the ordered list derived from the `ControlScheme` union, wrapping at both ends, and the row text announces the selected value;
   - Enter and pointer click activate the row and persist the selection to `ai_hell_settings`;
   - under `asteroids` the movement rows read **Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse**; under `fourDirectional` they read **Move Up / Move Down / Move Left / Move Right**;
   - both schemes share one binding set (rebinding under one scheme is visible under the other).
2. `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`:
   - with a saved `fourDirectional` setting, the spawned player ship uses four-directional movement (input maps to direct thrust, no turn keys);
   - with a saved `asteroids` setting, the spawned ship uses the Asteroids scheme;
   - the loaded ship-config object and `src/data/ship-config.csv` are not mutated by the resolution;
   - changing the setting mid-run does not alter the current run's ship (applies on the next spawn/run).

Use the existing `src/test/gameHarness.ts` boot helpers and the fake
localStorage helpers already used by `SettingsScene.test.ts` / `PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests are run through the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope) — never an ad-hoc runner invocation.

- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts` — row, cycling, persistence, relabelling, shared bindings.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — scheme application at spawn, config immutability, no mid-run change.

## Constraints

- Test-only change: no production code in this item.
- Boot real Phaser scenes via the shared harness; no bespoke mocks that bypass scene behaviour.
- Use UK English in descriptions and comments.

- `/skill:test` (changed scope) has been run and the red state is recorded in a comment.

## Parent AC coverage

AC5 (keyboard and pointer operable), AC6 (labels reflect the scheme) and AC8
(tests) from "Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player".

## Goal

As a player, I want to pick my control scheme in the Settings screen, with the
movement rows reading the way the chosen scheme actually behaves, so the ship
handles the way I expect.

## Scope

Extend the Controls section of `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts`:

- Add a focusable **Control Scheme** row whose options are iterated from the
  exported ordered scheme list (data-driven; no per-scheme UI branch), showing
  the current value in the row text.
- Left/Right cycles the scheme (wrapping), Enter and pointer click activate it,
  and the selection is persisted through the existing `_persist()` path.
- Relabel the movement rows for the selected scheme (Asteroids: **Thrust /
  Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse**; four-directional: **Move Up / Move
  Down / Move Left / Move Right**) while keeping the single shared binding set.
- Add test accessors (e.g. `getControlScheme()` / `setControlScheme()`)
  matching the existing accessor style used by tests.
- Keep the row inside the existing focus order so the screen stays fully
  keyboard operable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SettingsScene shows a Control Scheme control whose options are derived from the `ControlScheme` union (no hard-coded per-scheme UI branch) and displays the current value.
- The row is reachable via the existing focus order, changeable with Left/Right and Enter/click, and the selected value is announced in the row text.

## Goal

As a player, I want my saved control scheme applied to the ship so the run
actually handles the way I chose, taking effect on the next run/ship spawn
never mid-run.

## Scope

In `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, resolve the effective player scheme through the
shared helper when the player ship is created (the `new Player(...)` path in
`create()` / run setup) and pass it so the ship uses the scheme for that run.

- Read the stored setting from `ai_hell_settings` and the design default from
  the loaded ship config, then apply the resolved value to the created player.
- Never mutate the loaded ship-config object or `src/data/ship-config.csv`.
- Never call a live scheme swap on an existing ship mid-run; a change made in
  Settings while a run is active applies only to the next spawn/run.
- Leave the gyms on their own toggle-driven config path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayScene` creates the player ship with the resolved scheme: a saved `fourDirectional` setting drives four-directional input and a saved `asteroids` setting drives Asteroids input.
- Applying the scheme does not mutate `src/data/ship-config.csv` or the loaded ship-config object, and a change made mid-run does not alter the current run's ship.
- Scene tests from the scene-test item pass; `/skill:test` changed scope is green.
- Gyms keep their own scheme toggle (no forced scheme from settings).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — resolve and apply the scheme at player creation.
